image_prompt.text: Lockers, crawlspaces and low wall cutouts spread through the warren where a player breaks the killer's line of sight and hides
Large escape doors set into the outer boundary of the map, the way out once the tasks are done
Task stations placed all around the map — a machine or workbench a player walks up to and works at, sited so reaching them means crossing open ground

layout_placement.text: The escape doors in the outer boundary carry the round-win trigger
Separate start points for the killer and for the players, so the hunter and the hunted do not begin on top of each other
One trigger per task station, distributed across the whole map rather than clustered, so completing the set forces movement through the warren

mechanics: You try not to be killed by the killer
One player, or one character, is the killer hunting the others
Players complete tasks to progress the round
notes: Preset 1 vs All taken whole on its own shape warren-looping; P6 comes from the shape and is not overridden.

trigger-task is not in Survival's table or the universal six — taken from Simulation via options.md for the tasks the prompt names, with the wording bent from a job loop to objective stations under threat.

gate-escape is the assumed end of the run, inferred from the preset. The prompt never says how a round ends; if it is survive-the-timer instead, this option should come out (see the genre note that Disaster Survival deliberately has no exit).
The killer is assumed to be a player role, which is why spawn-protected is in and spawner-npc is not. If the killer is AI, swap them.

open_questions.ask: Is the killer another player, or an AI that patrols the map on its own? If it's a player I'll build separated start points for the two roles; if it's AI I'll build it an entry point and ground to patrol instead.
Once the tasks are finished, do the players escape through an exit — big doors set into the outer wall — or is there no way out and they just have to last until the round ends?
The tasks players do around the map: are those fixed stations you walk up to and use, like machines or workbenches, or items scattered on the floor to pick up and carry somewhere?
Nothing so far says how the place should look. Grimy industrial facility, dim horror house, bright stylized cartoon map, or somewhere modern and everyday?

skill_gap.name: no objective station under threat
skill_gap.why: The tasks are the only concrete thing this prompt names and Survival has no row for them. The 1 vs All preset is modelled on Flee the Facility and Survive the Killer, whose whole loop is working at objective stations while hunted, yet it ships cover-los, gate-escape and spawn-protected and nothing to work at. The nearest reachable row is Simulation's trigger-task, written as 'a station in a repeatable job loop — pickup, delivery, patient bed, planting plot', which is an economy loop rather than a timed objective under pursuit. It carries the right geometry and the wrong meaning, and it is only reachable by loading the whole catalogue.

notes_for_us: Genre files and options.md give IDs only — no Type (Flavor Name) — so emitting shape.type/shape.name and layout_placement.type forces a read of shapes.md or a second genre file even when the shortlist fits. I read one line of shapes.md for 'Looping Warren' and guessed 'Trigger' from the trigger-task ID prefix.

Step 4's sanctioned 'is there an end to this, or is it endless' question and step 5's 'never ask how the game is won' overlap badly here. Escape-through-a-gate versus outlast-a-timer decides whether gate-escape is built, so it is spatial, but it reads as a goal question and the brief bans the goal field.

Nothing says where to record that a preset option was inferred rather than asked for. notes is addressed to the pipeline and open_questions to a human, and gate-escape's provenance is neither; it only survives here because the record format has preset_derived.

The scale rule says the smallest thing that matters wins, but a chase map has prop-scale hiding spots and lockers and a building-scale warren to run through. Read literally, 'detail wins' lands on Room, which is too small for a map you run around. I took Block.

Survival's typical shapes list warren-looping but the genre file rewords only space-bounded, so the shape the genre's own flagship preset uses arrives with no Survival-flavoured sentence to lift into the offer.
